name: Acetyl tetrapeptide-3

lead: Acetyl tetrapeptide-3 is a cosmetic peptide used in hair-density topicals and is named as the hair-anchoring ingredient in Capixyl. It is usually combined with plant extracts.

One 24-week randomized, triple-blind trial in 32 people compared a combination of biochanin A, acetyl tetrapeptide-3 and ginseng extracts with 3% minoxidil solution in androgenetic alopecia, so the peptide's own effect was not isolated.

paras: Mechanistic claims are made by product makers; the studies reviewed here evaluated outcomes of the combination rather than the peptide's mechanism.
The trial assessed a safety profile for the combination as a stated objective [1]. It is a cosmetic ingredient rather than an approved hair-loss drug.

studies.title: An Herbal Extract Combination (Biochanin A, Acetyl tetrapeptide-3, and Ginseng Extracts) versus 3% Minoxidil Solution for the Treatment of Androgenetic Alopecia: A 24-week, Prospective, Randomized, Triple-blind, Controlled Trial.
studies.source: The Journal of clinical and aesthetic dermatology

lead: Acetyl tetrapeptide-3 is a cosmetic peptide used in topical hair products for thinning hair, commonly as part of the ingredient blend Capixyl, which also appears with biochanin A and ginseng extracts [1].

A 24-week randomized, triple-blind controlled trial in 32 men and women with mild to moderate androgenetic alopecia compared a combination of biochanin A, acetyl tetrapeptide-3 and ginseng extracts with 3% minoxidil solution [1]. A 2026 systematic review examined peptides for hair loss in clinical trials [2].

paras: The 24-week trial (N=32) randomized participants with mild to moderate androgenetic alopecia to twice-daily 1 mL applications of the herbal combination or 3% minoxidil, aiming to evaluate efficacy and safety [1]. Because the product combined three ingredients, results cannot be attributed to acetyl tetrapeptide-3 alone.
A 2026 systematic review searched PubMed, Embase and the Cochrane Library for clinical trials of peptide-containing therapies for hair loss and identified 14 studies out of 981 records [2].
